message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command to bring up the Docker daemon (the “Docker Engine”). It’s used to start *containers* that have already been created. If you want to start the Docker service on a Windows machine, you need to start the service that runs the Docker Engine – usually called **com.docker.service** – or launch Docker Desktop. Here are the typical ways to do it: | Method | How to run it | |--------|---------------| | **PowerShell** (recommended) | ```powershell
Start-Service -Name com.docker.service
``` | | **Command Prompt** | ```cmd
net start com.docker.service
``` | | **Docker Desktop GUI** | Double‑click the Docker Desktop icon from the Start menu or taskbar. | ### Why `docker start` won’t work - `docker start ` expects a container ID or name; it will error out if you give it something else. - Even if you had a container named `com.docker.service`, starting that container would not start the Docker Engine itself. ### Quick check After running one of the above commands, verify that the service is running: ```powershell Get-Service -Name com.docker.service ``` You should see its status as **Running**. Once the service is running, you can then use normal Docker CLI commands (`docker ps`, `docker run`, etc.) to interact with containers. --- #### TL;DR 1. **Do NOT** use `docker start` to start Docker itself. 2. Run `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` (or `net start com.docker.service`) in PowerShell/Command Prompt, or simply open Docker Desktop. 3. Verify with `Get-Service -Name com.docker.service` that it shows **Running**.

The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon itself. To start Docker service, you need to start the Docker Desktop or the Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. Or if using Docker Desktop, you might need to launch Docker Desktop application.

But the user wants to start Docker on Windows using docker start. That seems incorrect usage. We should explain that docker start starts containers, not the Docker engine. To start Docker engine, you need to start the Docker Desktop app or the Docker service. Provide commands like `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`.

We can also mention that if Docker Desktop is installed, you can start it via Start menu or by launching the executable. If using Docker Engine as a service, you can start it via PowerShell: `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`.

Also mention that you cannot start Docker engine from inside Docker container because it's host-level service.
